title: Reader chapter progress summary can wrap and inflate the navigation row
symptom: A long chapter progress summary in the reader bottom chapter-navigation row could wrap between the previous/next chapter buttons and increase the row height. A Pixel 8 / Android 14 Compose layout regression reproduced the issue at 320dp width: the progress text measured 60.571426dp high while the single-line navigation action measured 40dp.
root_cause: ReaderChapterNavigationRow rendered progressSummary with a plain Text inside a weighted middle slot. Unlike ReaderActionLabelText, it did not set maxLines, softWrap, or overflow, so fallback summaries that contain longer chapter titles could wrap and push the row taller.
fix: Constrained the chapter progress summary Text to one line.
Disabled soft wrapping and added ellipsis overflow so long summaries truncate inside the middle slot.
Added a Compose device regression that measures a long progress summary against a single-line navigation action in a narrow ReaderControls layout.
failed_attempts: Text presence assertions are not sufficient for this class of bug; the text can be present while still changing control height.
Assuming progress summaries are always short misses the formatter fallback path that can show a chapter title.
impact: Keeps the reader bottom chapter-navigation row visually stable when a real TXT produces a long fallback progress summary, reducing layout jumps around chapter controls.
